walkthrough:
Define the distribution of $X$, the number of people who enjoy Historical Drama:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}(160, 0.1)$$
Check the validity conditions for a normal approximation:
$$np = 160 \times 0.1 = 16 > 5, \quad np(1 - p) = 160 \times 0.1 \times 0.9 = 14.4 > 5$$

Calculate the mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$ for the approximating normal distribution $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$:
$$\mu = np = 160 \times 0.1 = 16$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 160 \times 0.1 \times 0.9 = 14.4 \implies \sigma = \sqrt{14.4}$$

Apply the continuity correction for the strict inequality $X > 17$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 17) = \mathrm{P}(X \ge 18) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y > 17.5)$$

Standardize to the standard normal variable $Z$ and compute the probability:
$$Z = \frac{17.5 - \mu}{\sigma} = \frac{17.5 - 16}{\sqrt{14.4}} = \frac{1.5}{3.7947} \approx 0.3953$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.3953) = 1 - \Phi(0.3953) = 1 - 0.6537 = 0.3463 \approx 0.346$$

teacher_walkthrough:
Start by identifying the exact distribution. The number of people $X$ out of $160$ who enjoy Historical Drama follows a binomial distribution:
$$X \sim \mathrm{B}(n, p) \quad \text{with } n = 160, \; p = 0.1$$
Check that the conditions for using a normal approximation are satisfied:
$$np = 160 \times 0.1 = 16 > 5$$
$$np(1 - p) = 160 \times 0.1 \times 0.9 = 14.4 > 5$$
Both conditions hold, so we approximate $X$ using a continuous normal random variable $Y \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$.

Calculate the parameters of the approximating normal distribution:
$$\mu = np = 160 \times 0.1 = 16$$
$$\sigma^2 = np(1 - p) = 16 \times 0.9 = 14.4 \implies \sigma = \sqrt{14.4} \approx 3.794733$$

Apply a continuity correction. The discrete inequality $X > 17$ means the integer values $18, 19, 20, \dots$.
In the continuous domain, the integer $18$ is represented by the interval $[17.5, 18.5]$, so values greater than $17$ correspond to $Y > 17.5$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 17) \approx \mathrm{P}(Y > 17.5)$$

Write down the standardization formula:
$$Z = \frac{Y - \mu}{\sigma}$$
Substitute $Y = 17.5$, $\mu = 16$, and $\sigma = \sqrt{14.4}$:
$$Z = \frac{17.5 - 16}{\sqrt{14.4}} = \frac{1.5}{3.794733} \approx 0.3953$$

Look up $z = 0.3953$ in the standard normal distribution table:
$$\Phi(0.395) = 0.6536, \quad \text{difference for } 3 \text{ is } 1 \implies \Phi(0.3953) = 0.6537$$
Calculate the upper tail area:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > 0.3953) = 1 - \Phi(0.3953) = 1 - 0.6537 = 0.3463 \approx 0.346$$
